details:
Q1: Which judge paths should run without host credentials in the isolated sandbox?
Choices:
A) Only the host Claude call for WAVE_JUDGE, STALL_JUDGE, INTEGRATION_JUDGE and SECURITY_JUDGE. The codex `danger-full-access` fallback stays on the host unchanged.
B) All four poller judges on both engines. Claude runs in the sandbox, and the codex path is replaced by OpenCode in a fresh sandbox (the RB_JUDGE pattern). No judge runs on the host with credentials. (RECOMMENDED)
C) Same as B, and also move the ORCHESTRATE decomposer (`orchestrate.yml`), which reads the author-controlled issue body, into the sandbox in the same change.
Q2: What should happen when the sandbox can't run (support scripts missing or outdated, preparation fails, or the transfer is rejected)?
Choices:
A) Defer the judge to the next poll tick and never fall back to the host. After N consecutive isolation failures on one tracking issue, mark the issue `ai:needs-human` and send a CRITICAL alert. N comes from a new variable, default 3, the same shape as `RB_JUDGE_ISOLATION_MAX_FAILURES`. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Defer the judge to the next poll tick and never fall back to the host, with no failure cap or escalation. Rely on the existing judge-failure CRITICAL alert.
C) Fall back to the current host codex path with a `::warning::`. This keeps judges running but leaves the credential exposure in place whenever isolation is down.
**Note:** C combined with Q1:B mostly undoes Q1:B. Picking both will require re-clarification.
Q3: Should the judges get read-only access, with every GitHub write done afterwards by deterministic code that checks their JSON verdict?
Choices:
A) Yes. All four judges get read-only sandbox access and nothing is transferred back. All issue, label and PR writes stay in the poller's existing deterministic code, which checks the parsed JSON verdict first. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Read-only for WAVE, STALL and SECURITY. INTEGRATION_JUDGE gets write access with validated transfer back (like the RB_JUDGE combined fix mode), so it can stage conflict edits.
